duplicateIntentAnalysis.method: For each product family, compare its own /software/{slug} page's measured impressions against the combined impressions of its /compare/{slug}-vs-X pages, to see how concentrated real demand is on the intended 'owner' page.

families.verdict: FRAGMENTATION_RISK (real, evidenced). Notion is the #1 most internally-linked product site-wide yet has zero ALTERNATIVE_GUIDES entry of its own.
Same fragmentation pattern as notion, at ~6x smaller volume.
NOT fragmented -- a SERP-override candidate, not a duplicate-intent problem.
NOT fragmented, and protected by an active experiment anyway -- do not touch.

duplicateIntentAnalysis.keyTakeaway: Having many comparison pages does not automatically cause cannibalization -- confluence/airtable/smartsheet all show 87-98% concentration on the intended page despite 3-7 comparison pages each. Notion and Trello are the two real, evidenced exceptions where demand is genuinely fragmented away from the product's own page.
